text:
Chris: Hi all, day 2 for me. Trying to build runtime inside the standard dev container on WSL2. Followed README but hitting ptxas "Value 'sm_89' is not valid" and then a linker failure `cannot find -lcuda`. Anyone seen this combo?

Chris: run: `docker run --gpus all -v /mnt/c/Users/chris/src:/src -w /src redwood/dev:cuda-12.2 make -j8`

Mika: welcome! :tada: sounds like a driver/toolkit mismatch + arch flag. Quick checks: `nvidia-smi` on host and `nvcc --version` in container. WSL often shows older Windows driver.

Natanael: also sm_89 is unusual; maybe someone set CUDAARCHS or the CMake defaults on your branch. Grep for sm_89 in the repo.

Chris: `nvidia-smi` on Windows shows Driver 515.65, container nvcc shows CUDA 12.2. Found sm_89 hardcoded in third_party/cuda_defs.cmake.

Rosie: Driver 515 < needed for CUDA12.2. Options: switch to redwood/dev:cuda-11.8 image or update Windows NVIDIA driver to latest WSL-supported version (we recommend 525+). For temp patch, change CUDAARCHS to sm_86 and remove the hardcoded sm_89.

Chris: switched image to cuda-11.8 and removed the sm_89 line, rebuild now. Linker now complaining `undefined reference to cuGetProcAddress`.

Mika: that API is from newer CUDA runtime. Likely a prebuilt third_party lib compiled against 12.x. Rebuild third_party libs or use matching toolkit.

Natanael: for WSL, also avoid bind-mounting from /mnt/c for heavy builds; copy repo into WSL filesystem and bind that to the container for performance and fewer path surprises.

Chris: copying into WSL FS and rebuilding with 11.8 fixed the undefined ref. Binary builds and starts. Thanks! Adding notes to onboarding doc about WSL driver+image mismatches and the sm_89 hardcode.

infra-bot: INFRA-468 opened: "Document WSL driver vs dev-image compatibility + scan repo for hardcoded CUDA archs"

Chris: appreciate the quick help. Tagging @Mika @Natanael if I run into CI flakiness related to this. :thumbsup:
